h: Jacob Confronts the Wisdom of Esau

p: מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ
— From the holy handwriting of the author:
בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עה, ד): "רַבָּנַן אָמְרֵי: מַלְאָכִים מַמָּשׁ".
— In Midrash Rabbah (Bereishit Rabbah 75:4): "The Rabbis say: actual heavenly angels."
וּמִסְּתָמָא "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים"
— And presumably both opinions—actual angels or human messengers—are the words of the living God (Eruvin 13b),
וְגַם: לְאֵיזֶה צֹרֶךְ שָׁלַח מַלְאָכִים לְעֵשָׂו?
— and furthermore one must ask: for what purpose did Jacob dispatch celestial angels to the wicked Esau?
אֲבָל בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (שָׁם עה, ג) אָמַר עוֹד:
— However, in Bereishit Rabbah (ibid., §3) it is further stated:
"לְדַרְכּוֹ הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ וְכוּלֵי",
— Jacob should not have provoked him, for Esau was going his own way, etc.,
וּכְמִתְרַעֲמִים עַל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁשָּׁלַח,
— the Sages seemingly taking issue with Jacob for sending messengers to him at all,
עַיֵּין שָׁם עַל פָּסוּק: "מַעְיָן נִרְפָּשׂ וּמָקוֹר מָשְׁחָת צַדִּיק מָט לִפְנֵי רָשָׁע" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, כו),
— see there, expounding the verse: "A troubled fountain and a corrupted spring is a righteous man who falters before the wicked" (Proverbs 25:26),
וְעַל פָּסוּק: "מַחֲזִיק בְּאָזְנֵי כָלֶב עֹבֵר מִתְעַבֵּר עַל רִיב לֹּא לוֹ" (שָׁם כו, יז),
— and upon the verse: "He who passes by and meddles with strife belonging not to him is like one that takes a dog by the ears" (Proverbs 26:17),
דְּעֵשָׂו נִקְרָא כֵּן (כֶּלֶב).
— for Esau is specifically designated as a dog.
וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב, פָּרָשָׁה פד, ה):
— And likewise in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Vayeshev, 84:5):
"מָשָׁל וְכוּלֵי כַּת שֶׁל כְּלָבִים וְכוּלֵי, כָּךְ וְכוּלֵי";
— "A parable of a pack of dogs that were barking at a traveler, etc., so too Esau and his chiefs";
וְכֵן (בְּסוֹף פָּרָשָׁה עז, ג): "כֶּלֶב אַגְרִיּוֹן וְכוּלֵי".
— and likewise in Bereishit Rabbah 77:3: "a fierce, wild dog (kelev agryon), etc."

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 75:4: “‘Messengers (malakhim)’ – these were flesh and blood messengers. The Rabbis say: Actual angels. Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said: Hagar was Sarah’s maidservant and five angels happened upon her, this one who is the beloved of the household, all the more so. If several angels escorted Eliezer, who was a slave of the household, this one, who was the beloved of the household, all the more so. Rabbi Yosei said: Joseph was the youngest of the tribes and three angels escorted him; that is what is written: ‘A man found him’ (Genesis 37:15), ‘the man asked him’ (Genesis 37:15), ‘the man said to him’ (Genesis 37:17); this one, who was the father of them all, all the more so. ‘Before him’ – before the one whose time to assume kingship was before his. Rabbi Yehoshua said: He removed his royal purple garment and cast it before him. He said to him: ‘Two starlings cannot sleep on one board.’ ‘To Esau his brother’ – although he is Esau, he is his brother. ‘To the land of Se’ir, the field of Edom’ – he is ruddy, his cooked food is red, his land is red, his mighty are red, his garment is red, and a red one will exact retribution from him in red garments. He is ruddy – ‘the first emerged ruddy’ (Genesis 25:25); ‘his cooked food is red’ – ‘feed me please from that red, red dish’ (Genesis 25:30); ‘his land is red’ – ‘to the land of Se’ir, the field of Edom’; ‘his mighty are red’ – ‘mighty ones are colored scarlet…’ (Nahum 2:4); and a red (adom) one will exact retribution from him – ‘my beloved is clear and ruddy (adom)’ (Song of Songs 5:10); in red garments – ‘why is there red on your garments?’ (Isaiah 63:2).”

h: Chaos and the World of Rectification

p: כִּי הוּא מֵעַזֵּי פָּנִים שֶׁבַּדּוֹר,
— For Esau embodies the insolent, brazen forces of the world,
שֶׁהֵם מִתְּתַקְעַ"ד (מִתְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שִׁבְעִים וְאַרְבָּעָה) דּוֹרוֹת,
— who originate from the 974 generations
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּחֲגִיגָה יד עַמּוּד א),
— as written in Chagigah (14a),
שֶׁהָיוּ רְאוּיִים לִהְיוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ,
— that were originally designated to be created during the two thousand years of Tohu (Chaos),
שֶׁהֵם מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ,
— stemming from the shattered Primordial World of Chaos (Olam HaTohu),
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע, הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְהָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— whence derives the root of all cosmic evil, the evil inclination, and the idolatrous nations, as is known.
וְעֵשָׂו – שֶׁמַּלְאָכוֹ סַמָּאֵ"ל שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ הַשְּׂטָנִים –
— And Esau—whose guardian angel is Samael, the chieftain of all the Satanic forces—
כֵּן עֵשָׂו שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָרַע שֶׁבְּכָל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.
— so too is Esau the physical root of all destructive powers latent across all the pagan nations.
וַעֲמָלֵק נִקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כד, כ),
— And Amalek, who issued from Esau, is termed "the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20),
וְהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע שֶׁבּוֹ מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ.
— for they are the concentrated root of the evil in him drawn directly from the World of Chaos.
וְעַל כֵּן נִרְמַז בְּפָרָשַׁת "אֵלֶּה הַמְּלָכִים" דֶּאֱדוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית לו, לא–לט):
— And for this reason, in the Torah portion of "These are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom" (Genesis 36:31–39),
"מַלְכִין קַדְמָאִין דְּמִיתוּ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאִדְרָא רַבָּא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קלה עַמּוּד א),
— "the primordial kings who died" (as written in the Idra Rabba, Zohar III 135a),
שֶׁהוּא סוֹד "בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָמוֹת וּמַחֲרִיבָן",
— which is the esoteric secret of God "creating worlds and destroying them",
שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט, ב) דְּרוֹמֵז לְעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ.
— which the Sages in Bereishit Rabbah (9:2) expounded as alluding to the shattering of the World of Chaos.
וְאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִידֵי פְּשׁוּטוֹ:
— And the text does not depart from its literal meaning:
דִּבְמַלְכֵי אֱדוֹם מְדַבֵּר,
— for it speaks of the literal kings of Edom,
שֶׁהֵם מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ שֶׁקָּדַם לְעוֹלַם הַתִּיקּוּן,
— who embodied the World of Chaos that historically and cosmically preceded the World of Rectification (Olam HaTikkun),
דְּזֶהוּ "לִפְנֵי מְלָךְ מֶלֶךְ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לו, לא).
— which is the inner meaning of "before there reigned any king over the children of Israel" (Genesis 36:31).

p: וְרוֹמֵז עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא מֶלֶךְ,
— And this "king" alludes to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is titled a king,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּזְבָחִים קב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א, וּבְמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת כ, ב)
— as stated in Zevachim (102a) and in Midrash Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Acharei Mot 20:2)
גַּבֵּי אֱלִישֶׁבַע: "יְבָמָהּ – מֶלֶךְ",
— concerning Elisheva daughter of Amminadab: "her brother-in-law (Moses) was a king",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ב, ו) עַל פָּסוּק: "וַיְהִי בִישֻׁרוּן מֶלֶךְ" (דְּבָרִים לג, ה);
— and as expounded on the verse: "And he was king in Jeshurun" (Deuteronomy 33:5);
כִּי בִּפְשׁוּטוֹ, מֶלֶךְ הָאַחֲרוֹן (הֲדַר) לֹא כָּתוּב בּוֹ מִיתָה
— for according to the simple text, regarding the last king of Edom (Hadar, Genesis 36:39) death is not recorded,
לְפִי שֶׁעֲדַיִן הָיָה חַי בִּזְמַן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
— because he was still alive during the generation of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him;
וְעַל כֵּן בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א א, נא) נֶאֱמַר גַּם עָלָיו מִיתָה: "וַיָּמָת הֲדַד".
— and therefore in the Book of Chronicles, composed later, death is recorded of him as well: "And Hadad died" (I Chronicles 1:51).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי גְּמַר עוֹלַם הַתִּיקּוּן הוּא בְּקַבָּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַתּוֹרָה,
— And the reason is that the culmination of the World of Rectification transpired through Israel receiving the Torah at Sinai,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג עַמּוּד א) דְּאִלְמָלֵא קִבְּלוּ, הָיָה מַחֲזִיר עוֹלָם לְתֹהוּ.
— as stated in Avodah Zarah (3a) that had Israel not accepted the Torah, God would have returned the entire universe back to Chaos.
וְאַף דְּהַתְחָלַת שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּשֶׁהָיָה בֶּן נ"ב (חֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם) שָׁנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם ט עַמּוּד א),
— And even though the two thousand years of Torah began with our father Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was fifty-two years old, as stated in Avodah Zarah (9a),
אָז הָיָה הַתְחָלַת בִּנְיַן עוֹלַם הַתִּיקּוּן, אֲבָל הַשְׁלָמָתוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
— that marked merely the inception of building the World of Rectification, whereas its absolute completion was achieved at the Giving of the Torah.

p: וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ג, ה) עַל פָּסוּק "יְהִי אוֹר", וּ(פָּרָשָׁה סד, ח) גַּבֵּי בְּאֵרוֹת דְּיִצְחָק אָמַר:
— And in Bereishit Rabbah (3:5 on "Let there be light," and 64:8 on the wells of Isaac) it states:
"בְּסֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית נִתְעַסֵּק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּבָרָא עוֹלָמוֹ",
— “The Holy One, blessed be He, engaged Himself in the Book of Genesis and created His world,”
מְבוֹאָר דְּכָל הַסֵּפֶר הוּא מִבְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם, וְלֹא פָּרָשַׁת דְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית בִּלְבַד;
— clarifying that the entire Book of Genesis deals with the creation of the cosmos, not merely the opening section of the Creation;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל הַסִּפּוּרִים דְּשָׁם – מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה, וּסְדוֹם, וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל, וְעֵשָׂו וּמִשְׁפַּחְתָּם –
— meaning that all the historical narratives recorded therein—concerning the Generation of the Flood, the Generation of the Dispersion, Sodom, Ishmael, Esau and their families—
הַכֹּל מִבְּרִיאַת עוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ וַחֲשׁוֹכָא דְּקָדַם לִנְהוֹרָא וְעוֹלַם הַתִּיקּוּן.
— all portray the unfolding of the World of Chaos and the darkness that precedes light, leading into the World of Rectification.
וְי"ב (שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה) פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת בְּסֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית:
— Now there are twelve parashiyot in the Book of Genesis:
וּשְׁתֵּי רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, בְּרֵאשִׁית וְנֹחַ, הֵם מִשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ, שֶׁהוּא מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ לְבַד;
— and the first two, Bereishit and Noach, belong chronologically to the two thousand years of Chaos, portraying the World of Chaos alone;
וּפָרָשַׁת לֶךְ לְךָ מַתְחִיל מֵ"הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ה), שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מִגְּמָרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ט עַמּוּד א);

— while Parashat Lekh Lekha begins from "the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (when Abraham was fifty-two), which marks the dawn of the two thousand years of Torah, as cited above from Avodah Zarah;
וְהֵם עֶשֶׂר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת עַד סוֹף הַסֵּפֶר, שֶׁהֵם בִּנְיַן עוֹלַם הַתִּיקּוּן,
— and the remaining ten parashiyot until the end of Genesis constitute the systematic construction of the World of Rectification,
וְסִפּוּרִים מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ שֶׁהָיוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן, שֶׁהֵם "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" וְנִבְנוּ גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגְדָּם.
— alongside the manifestations of the World of Chaos contemporaneous with them, standing "one opposite the other" and built in dynamic counterpoint.

p: וּסְדוֹם – שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשְּׁבִירָה שֶׁנֶּגֶד תִּיקּוּן דְּאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק – נֶאֶבְדוּ;
— And Sodom—which was the shattered dross standing directly opposite the holy rectifications of Abraham and Isaac—was utterly eradicated;
אֲבָל עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל, שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵיהֶם נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— however, Esau and Ishmael, who both stand counterposed against our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
וְהֵם כּוֹלְלִים כָּל שִׁבְעִים (אוּמּוֹת) – זֶה ל"ה (שְׁלֹשִׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה) מִיָּמִין וְזֶה ל"ה מִשְּׂמֹאל כַּיָּדוּעַ –
— and who encompass all seventy nations—thirty-five on the right through Ishmael and thirty-five on the left through Esau, as is known—

הֵם בִּנְיַן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנִּשְׁאָר מִשְּׁבִירַת עוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ, לְצֹרֶךְ הַבְּחִירָה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, עַל יְדֵי מְצִיאוּת הָרַע דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע וְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.

— constitute the surviving root-structure salvaged from the shattering of Chaos, preserved specifically for the sake of free choice in this world granted to Israel, via the reality of the evil inclination and the idolatrous nations.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Da’at Tevunot, §124: “Evil considered by itself is nothing but corruption, loss, and destruction. Yet in conjunction with the other arrangements, on the contrary, benefit flows from it to the person himself, for all merit and the possibility of service depend upon it. It stands there to be conquered, not to conquer: its existence is only so that the person should cut it away, like the stone standing at a crossroads in the Midrashic parable cited above. … Before this work is completed, although evil also stands for the person’s benefit—to be conquered by him—it can, Heaven forbid, be to his detriment if he does not conquer it, for then evil will prevail rather than rectification. But after the work is completed and evil is abolished, the tranquility of the whole creation will be everlasting and will never cease.”

p: וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִתְבַּשֵּׂר: "וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְצָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יד) –
— And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, was promised: "And you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south" (Genesis 28:14)—
נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים (שַׁבָּת קיח עַמּוּד ב),
— an unbounded heritage without borders (Shabbat 118b),
שֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לִכְבּוֹשׁ כָּל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
— meaning that he is destined to subjugate all the nations of the world,
כִּי יְבוֹעַר כָּל הָרַע וְיֵצֶר הָרָע עַל יָדוֹ,
— for all evil and the evil inclination will be eradicated through him,
כִּי הוּא וְזַרְעוֹ גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן.
— since he and his seed embody the final completion of Rectification.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִיתַּן בִּגְבוּל, רַק אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
— In contrast, to Abraham and Isaac the inheritance was given with strict boundaries, encompassing the Land of Israel alone,
כִּי לֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא עַד יַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם פְּסֹלֶת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּשַׁבָּת קמו עַמּוּד א).
— because the primordial defilement had not yet ceased until Jacob, as dross still emerged from them, as written in Shabbat (146a).
וְאַף דִּבְאֶמֶת יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו לֹא נִקְרָא זַרְעָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּנְדָרִים לא עַמּוּד א: "כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע – וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק"),
— And even though in essential truth Ishmael and Esau are not halakhically considered their seed, as stated in Nedarim (31a): "'For in Isaac shall your seed be called'—and not all of Isaac",
זֶה נִתְבָּרֵר אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְחַר יַעֲקֹב.
— this absolute separation was established only after Jacob was chosen.

p: וְאֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן: "בַּכֹּל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כד, א), "מִכֹּל" (שָׁם כז, לג),
— Now concerning Abraham and Isaac, Scripture uses the qualified expressions: bakol ("in all," Genesis 24:1) and mikol ("of all," Genesis 27:33),
שֶׁלָּמְדוּ מִזֶּה (בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא טז–יז):
— from which the Sages derived (at the end of the first chapter of Bava Batra 16b–17a):
שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן יֵצֶר הָרָע, וּמַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, וְרִמָּה וְתוֹלֵעָה, וְשֶׁטָּעֲמוּ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא;
— that the evil inclination, the Angel of Death, and worms held no dominion over them, and that they tasted a foretaste of the World to Come;
וְהוּא כִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְאֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בִּבְרָכוֹת נז עַמּוּד ב).
— which mirrors the sanctity of Shabbat, being a foretaste of the World to Come and one-sixtieth of it (Berakhot 57b).
וּנְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה – דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בָּהּ כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (חֵלֶק ב, פח עַמּוּד ב) – וְהַיְינוּ בְּלֹא יֵצֶר הָרָע.
— And the additional soul of Shabbat—wherein all spiritual perfection resides after the manner of the World to Come (Zohar II 88b)—operates entirely without the evil inclination.
וּמִי שֶׁמֵּת בְּשַׁבָּת, וַדַּאי אֵין הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה יוֹצְאָה עַל יְדֵי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת כְּלָל.
— And for one who departs this world on Shabbat, the additional soul certainly does not exit via the Angel of Death at all.
אֲבָל אֶצְלָם נֶאֱמַר "בַּכֹּל", "מִכֹּל", וְלֹא "כֹּל" מַמָּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיַעֲקֹב:
— However, regarding Abraham and Isaac it states bakol and mikol, and not absolute kol (all) as stated of Jacob;
וְיִצְחָק זָכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי הַסְּעוּדָה שֶׁהֶאֱכִילוֹ יַעֲקֹב, דְּאָמַר אָז: "וָאֹכַל מִכֹּל", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר שֶׁהוּא כִּקְדוּשַּׁת אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת;
— for Isaac attained this state specifically through the meal Jacob fed him, exclaiming: "and I have eaten of all (mikol)," which was imbued with the holiness of the Shabbat meals;

p: וְהָיָה בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו, וְעוֹד מִקּוֹדֶם, מִיָּד בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵאָבִיו כְּשֶׁהָיָה בֶּן ס"ג (שִׁשִּׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ) שָׁנִים, הִבְטִיחוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "וּפָרַצְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר";
— And this applied during his father's lifetime, and even earlier: the moment he departed from his father at age sixty-three, the Holy One promised him: "And you shall spread abroad, etc.";
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ: "אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵךְ" (שָׁם כח, טו) –
— and this was fulfilled through the divine guarantee: "Behold, I am with you, and will keep you in all places where you go" (Genesis 28:15)—
שֶׁהֻבְטַח שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרֶנּוּ מִכָּל רָע, וְלֹא יִתְעֶה אַחַר יֵצֶר הָרָע, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא "וּפָרַצְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר".
— being promised that Hashem would preserve him from all evil so that he would never stray after the evil inclination, whereupon "and you shall spread abroad" followed naturally.
כִּי נִיצוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא גַּם כֵּן נִיצוּחַ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
— For the subduing of the evil inclination is fundamentally identical to the subduing of the idolatrous nations,
שֶׁכָּל אוּמָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ כֹּחַ רַע מְיוּחָד, וְקִיבּוּצָם הֵם כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָרַע דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע.
— since every nation embodies a specific trait of evil, and their totality comprises all the forces of the yetzer hara.

p: וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יא, ז):
— And in Bereishit Rabbah (11:7):
דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, יָרַשׁ הָעוֹלָם בְּמִדָּה;
— Abraham our father, concerning whom explicit Sabbath observance is not written in Scripture, inherited the world with bounded measure;
וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת – דִּכְתִיב: "וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח) – יָרַשׁ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִדָּה וְכוּלֵי.
— whereas Jacob, concerning whom Sabbath observance is written—"and he encamped (va-yichan) before the city" (Genesis 33:18)—inherited the world without measure.
וְאַף דְּגַם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קִיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה (יוֹמָא כח עַמּוּד ב),
— And even though Abraham our father likewise fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given,
וְגִרְסַת הָרַשְׁבָּ"א וְסֵפֶר הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל: "אֲפִילּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין", וְאִם כֵּן שָׁמַר גַּם תְּחוּמִין –
— the text in the Rashba and Sefer HaEshkol reading "even the eruv of Shabbat travel boundaries," such that Abraham observed the limits of the Sabbath as well—
אֲבָל אֵין עַל זֶה רֶמֶז בַּכָּתוּב;
— nonetheless there is no explicit textual hint to this in the biblical verse;
וּדְיַעֲקֹב רָמוּז בַּתּוֹרָה,
— whereas Jacob's Sabbath rest is explicitly encoded within the Torah text.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה – הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה בּוֹ בִּקְבִיעוּת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
— And that which is inscribed in the Written Torah signifies that this sanctity is fixed within him permanently for all eternity;
דְּהַתּוֹרָה נִצְחִית וְנִקְרֵאת "אֱמֶת", וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב ("תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב"),
— for the Torah is eternal and termed Truth, which is likewise the sefirotic attribute of Jacob,
וֶ"אֱמֶת" נִקְרָא מַה שֶּׁתִּכּוֹן לָעַד, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד עִמּוֹ וְשׁוֹמְרוֹ מִכָּל רָע,
— and Truth denotes that which endures forever—that Hashem is eternally with him to shield him from all evil—
וְעַל כֵּן מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה דְּכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו כֵּן.
— and therefore his bed is whole, all his offspring sharing this eternal status.
וְהֻבְטַח "וּפָרַצְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר" שֶׁכְּבָר פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא;
— And he was promised "and you shall spread abroad," for in him the defilement ceased;
אֲבָל אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, אַף דְּמִצַּד עַצְמָם זָכוּ גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וּבִיטּוּל יֵצֶר הָרָע,
— whereas Abraham and Isaac, although in their own personal righteousness they tasted the World to Come and the nullification of the evil inclination,
זֶהוּ רַק מִצִּדָּם, וּמִצַּד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁעָתִיד לָצֵאת מֵהֶם,
— that was solely their private personal attainment, and because of our father Jacob who was destined to emerge from them;
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת סג, ב) עַל פָּסוּק: "יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם" (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כב) –
— in line with what is written in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 63:2) on the verse: "Jacob who redeemed Abraham" (Isaiah 29:22)—
דְּעַל יָדוֹ נִיצּוֹל מִכִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ,
— that Abraham was saved from Nimrod's fiery furnace through the future merit of Jacob,
מָשָׁל וְכוּלֵי שֶׁצָּפָה שֶׁיּוֹלִיד בַּת שֶׁתִּנָּשֵׂא לַמֶּלֶךְ וְכוּלֵי.
— a parable of one saved from execution because the king foresaw that he would father a daughter who would marry the king.
וְהַיְינוּ כֵּיוָן דְּלֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא מֵהֶם עֲדַיִן, וְיָצָא גַּם כֵּן פְּסֹלֶת.
— For the primordial defilement had not yet ceased from their physical loins, so that dross still emerged from them.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 63:2: “‘The crown of elders is grandchildren’ (Proverbs 17:6). The fathers are the crown of their children, and the children are the crown of their fathers. The fathers are the crown of their children, as it is stated: ‘And the glory of children is their fathers’ (Proverbs 17:6). And the children are the crown of their fathers, as it is written: ‘The crown of elders is grandchildren.’ Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said: Abraham was rescued from the fiery furnace due only to the merit of Jacob. This is analogous to one who had a judgment before the governor, and his sentence, issued by the governor, was that he was to be burned. That governor foresaw through astrology that he (the defendant) was destined to beget a daughter and she would marry the king. He said: ‘He is worthy to be spared due to the merit of his daughter that he is destined to beget, and she will marry the king.’ So, Abraham, his sentence issued by Nimrod was that he was to be burned. The Holy One blessed be He foresaw that Jacob was destined to emerge from him. He said: ‘Abraham is worthy of being spared due to the merit of Jacob.’ That is what is written: ‘Therefore, so says the Lord to the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham…’ (Isaiah 29:22). Alternatively, ‘the crown of elders is grandchildren’ – ‘this is the legacy of Isaac, Abraham’s son.’”

p: וְהֲגַם דְּהֻבְטְחוּ בְּנַחֲלַת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא שִׁבְעָה אוּמּוֹת הַכּוֹלְלִים כָּל שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת הָרַע,
— And even though Abraham and Isaac were promised the Land of Israel, which encompasses seven Canaanite nations embodying the seven unholy emotional traits,
וְהֵם שְׁלֵמִים בְּכָל שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת – הֵם רַק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
— and Abraham and Isaac perfected these seven traits, that was achieved only at the root-level.
כִּי שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת יֵשׁ, הַיְינוּ כָּל אֶחָד מִשֶּׁבַע כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה;
— For there are seventy nations, each of the seven comprising ten Sefirot, forming a complete stature (7 × 10 = 70);
וְאוֹתָן שִׁבְעָה עַמְמִין דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם הַכְּתָרִים דְּרַע, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׁרָשִׁים שֶׁל כָּל מִדָּה;
— and those seven nations of Canaan represent the unholy crowns (Keter) of evil, the supernal roots of each trait;
וְאַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק הֻבְטְחוּ רַק עַל נִיצוּחַ הַכְּתָרִים הַשָּׁרָשִׁים, שֶׁהֵם מוּשְׁרָשִׁים בְּטוֹב בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ;
— and Abraham and Isaac were promised victory merely over those root-crowns, which are rooted in goodness at their supernal source;
אֲבָל מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לֹא נִתְבָּרְרוּ עַד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
— but throughout the outward branches and practical expansion they were not refined until Jacob whose bed is whole,
דְּבֵירֵר כָּל קוֹמַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִיצוּחַ כָּל קוֹמַת הָרַע בְּכָל שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת.
— who refined the entire Stature of Holiness, thereby subduing the entire Stature of Evil across all seven attributes.
וְהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת צוּרַת הָאָדָם,
— And Jacob embodies the complete archetypal form of Man (Tzurat HaAdam),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עח, ג) דְּאִיקוֹנִין שֶׁלּוֹ בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah on this portion: that his visage is engraved upon the Throne of Glory,
דְּהוּא צוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, כו).
— which is the divine "likeness as the appearance of a man upon the throne" (Ezekiel 1:26).
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת סא עַמּוּד א): "אַתֶּם קְרוּיִם אָדָם",
— Therefore the Sages declared (Yevamot 61a): "You, Israel, are called Adam",
דְּאָדָם מוֹלִיד אָדָם, וְכָל זַרְעוֹ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שְׁלֵימוּת צוּרַת אָדָם;
— for Man begets Man, and all of Jacob's descendants inherit this intrinsic human form;
דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא", כְּ"אָסָא דְּבֵינֵי הִיזְמֵי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין מד עַמּוּד א),
— for "even though he has sinned, he remains Israel"—like a fragrant myrtle standing among thorns (Sanhedrin 44a)—
דְּמַה שֶּׁבְּעֶצֶם וְלֹא בְּמִקְרֶה לֹא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה בַּזֶּרַע, דְּאָדָם לֹא יוֹלִיד בְּהֵמָה.
— for that which is essential and not accidental can never change in the seed, since Man cannot beget an animal.
וְכָל שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת חִבּוּר אֶחָד,
— And all three Patriarchs form one unified bond,
דְּמַעֲלַת יַעֲקֹב רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ גַּם מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, וְהוּא "חוּט הַמְשֻׁלָּשׁ";
— for Jacob's preeminence exists because he synthesizes the attributes of Abraham and Isaac, forming the threefold cord;
וְעִם זַרְעוֹ הֵם קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה דְּתִיקּוּן.
— and together with his children they comprise the complete Stature of Rectification.

p: וּמִן פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב עַד סוֹף הַסֵּפֶר אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת הֵם:
— And from Parashat Vayeshev until the conclusion of Genesis are four parashiyot:
תִּיקּוּן נְהִי"ם (נֵצַח, הוֹד, יְסוֹד, מַלְכוּת),
— corresponding to the rectification of the lower Sefirot: Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malchut,
וּמְסַיֵּים בִּקְבוּרַת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ;
— and the Book concludes with the burial of Joseph, who represents the perfection of Tzaddik, Yesod Olam, for which he was the chariot;
וְהַשְּׁלֵימוּת הוּא אַחַר מִיתָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תּוֹלְדוֹת ז)
— and this absolute perfection is confirmed only after death, as stated in Midrash Tanchuma (Toldot 7)
דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְיַיחֵד שְׁמוֹ עַל צַדִּיקִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם, דְּאוּלַי יֶחֶטְאוּ.
— that the Holy One does not attach His Name to living tzaddikim, lest they falter.
וּשְׁלֵימוּת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן לְגַמְרֵי –
— And the final perfection of the attribute of Malchut, which is the absolute completion of cosmic rectification—
זֶה יִהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
— this will be realized solely through King Messiah,
שֶׁהוּא מַלְכוּת דְּלָא יִתְחַבַּל לְעָלְמִין (דָּנִיֵּאל ז, יד),
— whose kingdom is an everlasting dominion that shall not be destroyed,
וִיבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת וְכָל הָרַע, וְאָז יְקוּיַּם "וּפָרַצְתָּ",
— when death and evil are swallowed up forever, and "and you shall spread abroad" is fulfilled;
וְלֹא נִשְׁלַם עֲדַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דְּעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל עֲבוֹדַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
— which is not yet consummated in this world, for toward this goal all human service in this world is directed.

וְרַק בְּבִרְכַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּפָרָשַׁת וַיְחִי לַשְּׁבָטִים, וְלִיהוּדָה בִּפְרָט, שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ עַל הַמַּלְכוּת: "לֹא יָסוּר וְגוֹמֵר וְלוֹ יִקְּהַת עַמִּים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מט, י) –

— And only in Jacob's blessings in Parashat Vayechi to the tribes, and to Judah in particular, promising him eternal sovereignty: "The scepter shall not depart... and unto him shall the gathering of the people be"—
בָּזֶה רָמוּז תִּיקּוּן הַמַּלְכוּת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת לְעֵת קֵץ;
— is the ultimate perfection of Malchut at the End of Days hinted;
וְהוּא שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ לְגַלּוֹת אָז וְנִסְתַּם מִמֶּנּוּ (פְּסָחִים נו עַמּוּד א),
— and this is what Jacob sought to disclose before it was hidden from him,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ סְתוּמִים וַחֲתוּמִים הַדְּבָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדָנִיֵּאל (יב, ט),
— for Hashem willed that these secrets be closed and sealed as written in Daniel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק, סַנְהֶדְרִין צט עַמּוּד א): "לְלִבִּי גִּלִּיתִי וְכוּלֵי",
— and as stated in Sanhedrin (99a): "To My heart alone have I revealed it";
וְעַל כֵּן גַּם כָּאן רָמוּז בְּסָתוּם וְחָתוּם.
— and therefore here too it remains veiled in concealment.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 7: “You find that everyone who becomes blind is considered as though dead. How do we know this? R. Simeon the son of Yohai said: The Holy One, blessed be He, never associates His name with righteous men during their lifetimes. He waits until they have died, as it is said: As for the holy that are in the earth, they are the excellent in whom is all My delight (Ps. 16:3). When are men regarded as truly holy? Only after they have been buried in the earth. During their lifetimes, however, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not associate His name with theirs. And why not? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is not certain whether or not the evil inclination within them will ultimately lead them astray. When they are dead, however, He does couple His name with theirs. Nevertheless, we find that the Holy One, blessed be he, did couple his name with that of the righteous Isaac during his lifetime, when he said to Jacob: I am the Lord, the God of Abraham, thy father, and the God of Isaac (Gen. 28:43). R. Berechiah and the rabbis discussed this matter. The rabbis maintained that He considered Isaac’s ashes as though they were heaped upon the altar, while R. Berechiah insisted that he was considered as dead because he had already lost his sight. Because of his blindness he remained secluded within his home, and the result was that the evil inclination departed from him. Hence it is written: And it came to pass that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim (Gen. 27:1).”

p: וּבָזֶה נִשְׁלַם סֵדֶר בִּנְיַן הָעוֹלָם וְעֵסֶק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ:
— And with this the construction of the universe and Hashem's cosmic design are fulfilled:
כִּי מִשֶּׁבָּאוּ שִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם שִׁבְעִים כֹּחוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה נֶגֶד כֹּחוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה דְּשִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת,
— for once the seventy souls of Jacob entered Egypt, embodying seventy holy forces counterbalancing the seventy impure nations,
הֲרֵי נִשְׁלַם הַכֹּל "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה".
— the entire matrix of "one opposite the other" stood complete.
וְ"כַלְבִּין דַּחֲצִיפִין" שֶׁמֵּעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ, דְּנָטְלִין לְבַר מִבְּנֵי הֵיכָלָא דִּכְסִיפִין לְמֶחֱזֵי זִיוֵיהּ דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין, שֶׁהוּא צוּרַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
— And the "insolent dogs" of Chaos are banished outside from the children of the palace who yearn to gaze upon the splendor of Ze'ir Anpin, which is the countenance of our father Jacob;
וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (חֵלֶק ב, פח עַמּוּד ב) דְּאַסְּעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית נֶאֱמַר: "וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ" (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד),
— and in Zohar Yitro it is taught that of the Third Meal it is written: "and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father",
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַסְּעוּדָה שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהוּא זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים,
— for this Third Meal belongs to Ze'ir Anpin as written in Pri Etz Chaim,
וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח עַמּוּד ב) מַיְיתֵי עַל זֶה קְרָא דְּ"וּפָרַצְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר",
— and the Gemara (Shabbat 118b) adduces on this the verse "and you shall spread abroad",
שֶׁזֶּהוּ נַחֲלָתוֹ לִכְבּוֹשׁ כָּל שִׁבְעִים אוּמּוֹת וְכָל הָעוֹלָם,
— for his unbounded heritage is to subdue all seventy nations and the entire world,
וּלְדַחוֹתָם לְנוּקְבָא דִּתְהוֹמָא רַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַתֹּהוּ הַקּוֹדֵם לַתִּיקּוּן – דְּ"חֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם", עַד שֶׁאָמַר "יְהִי אוֹר", דְּהוּא הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה.
— casting them into the abyss of the Great Deep—the primal Chaos of "darkness upon the face of the deep" prior to "Let there be light," which is Rectification through the Torah.

p: וְסֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית עֵסֶק הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
— The Book of Genesis portrays the creation of the nation of Israel,
וְהוּא בִּנְיַן הָאוֹר שֶׁהֵם הַכְּלִי קִיבּוּל לָאוֹר,
— fashioning the vessels capable of containing the divine light;
וְנַפְשׁוֹתָם הוּא הָאוֹר עַצְמוֹ, כִּי נַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה;
— their souls being the light itself, derived from the letters of the Torah;
וּכְלַל הַתּוֹרָה כ"ב (עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם) אוֹתִיּוֹת:
— the Torah comprising twenty-two letters:
ג' (שָׁלֹשׁ) אִמּוֹת אֶמֶ"שׁ הֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת,
— three Mother letters (Alef, Mem, Shin) corresponding to the three Patriarchs,
וְי"ב (שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה) פְּשׁוּטוֹת י"ב שְׁבָטִין,
— twelve Simple letters corresponding to the twelve Tribes,
וְז' (שֶׁבַע) כְּפוּלוֹת שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה;
— and seven Double letters corresponding to the seven days of Creation (Sefer Yetzirah);
וְשִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ הֵם שִׁבְעִים אַנְפִּין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שֶׁהוּא שִׁבְעִים כֹּחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה;
— and the seventy souls correspond to the seventy facets of the Torah, embodying seventy holy soul-faculties;
וּמִזֶּה הוּא כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית מז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב):
— from which all Creation is sustained, as written in the Zohar (I 47b):
דְּשָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ עוֹבָדָא וְאוּמָּנוּתָא דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְשֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְכָל צְבָאָם אִלֵּין פְּרָטֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שִׁבְעִים פָּנִים לַתּוֹרָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— that heaven and earth are the handiwork of the Written and Oral Torah, and all their host are the seventy facets of Torah, see there.

Abba says, it is the Garden of Eden, which God has cunningly wrought upon the earth after the supernal pattern for the righteous to seize and hold ; hence it is written ‘before the sons of men’, since this one is in the presence of men, while the other is in the presence of the holy angels. R. Simeon said: ‘The Garden of Eden above is said to be ‘before the sons of men’ because in it are gathered the righteous who perform the will of their Master’. Simeon said: ‘These words designate the general fabric of the Written Law, and the general fabric of the Oral Law. The words AND ALL THEIR HOSTS designate the details of the Torah, the seventy alternative explanations of the Torah; while the words AND THEY WERE COMPLETED imply that the two Torahs are complementary to one another. Or again, ‘heaven and earth’ may be interpreted as the general and the particular, and ‘all their hosts’ as the inner meanings of the Torah, its rules concerning clean and unclean, etc.”

AND WERE FINISHED: implying that all the work which was to be done, both above and below, was finished. THE HEAVEN AND THE EARTH: above and below. R. Simeon said: ‘These words designate the general fabric of the Written Law, and the general fabric of the Oral Law. The words AND ALL THEIR HOSTS designate the details of the Torah, the seventy alternative explanations of the Torah; while the words AND THEY WERE COMPLETED imply that the two Torahs are complementary to one another. Or again, ‘heaven and earth’ may be interpreted as the general and the particular, and ‘all their hosts’ as the inner meanings of the Torah, its rules concerning clean and unclean, etc.”

p: וְסֵפֶר שְׁמוֹת הוּא הֲוָיוֹת הָאוֹר וְהִתְגַּלּוּתוֹ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה;
— The Book of Exodus depicts the actualization and disclosure of this light at Sinai;
וּמַתְחִיל בְּמִיתַת כָּל הַדּוֹר הַהוּא דְּבָאֵי מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהֵם גְּמַר בְּרִיאַת הָאוֹר וּתְחִלַּת יְצִירָתוֹ;
— opening with the passing of that entire generation who came into Egypt, marking the culmination of the creation of the light and the dawn of its formation;
וְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הוּא עִיבּוּר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי" (דְּבָרִים ד, לד) – כְּעוּבָּר הַנִּשְׁמָט מִמְּעֵי אִמּוֹ.
— and the exile in Egypt was like gestation, "a nation from the midst of another nation" resembling a fetus extracted from the womb.
וְאָז חָזַר הַתֹּהוּ כִּתְחִלַּת הַבְּרִיאָה,
— And then Chaos seemed to reemerge as at the beginning of Creation,
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמו עַמּוּד א) דְּלֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא עַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה;
— which is why the Talmud states that their defilement did not cease until the Giving of the Torah;
וְשָׁם אָמְרוּ דִּפְלִיגֵי, וְ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" כְּכָל פְּלוּגְתָּתָם:
— and both opinions are the words of the living God:
דִּבְאֶמֶת מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא;
— for in their inner essence, defilement ceased from Jacob onward whose bed was whole;
אֲבָל אַף דְּהֵם מִצַּד עַצְמָם שְׁלֵמִים, עַל יְדֵי הֶיקֵּף זוּהֲמַת מִצְרַיִם מִכָּל צַד הָיוּ כְּעוּבָּר שֶׁהוּא יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ, וּכְאִלּוּ גַּם מֵהֶם לֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא.
— yet being surrounded by the filth of Egypt on all sides, they were like a fetus considered part of its mother's thigh, appearing as though defilement had not ceased.
וּבֶאֱמֶת זֶה הָיָה לְצֹרֶךְ גִּידּוּל הָאוֹר כְּעוּבָּר הַגָּדֵל בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ,
— Yet this enclosure was necessary for the maturation of the light, like a fetus growing in the womb,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק: "בְּחֹמֶר וּבִלְבֵנִים" – דָּא קַל וָחֹמֶר וְלִיבּוּן הִלְכְתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א).
— as expounded in the Zohar: "in mortar and in bricks"—this is the dialectic reasoning of kal vachomer and clarifying halakhah.
וּבִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם נִתְגַּלָּה וְנוֹלַד הָאוֹר וְיָצָא לַפּוֹעַל,
— And at the Exodus the light was born into manifest actuality,
וְעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא יֶחֱרַץ כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת יא, ז) – הֵם דּוֹרוֹת הַתֹּהוּ.
— wherefore it was said: "not a dog shall move its tongue" (Exodus 11:7)—dogs embodying the chaotic forces of Tohu.

h: Sending Esau a Call to Repentance

p: וְעִנְיַן "מַלְאָכִים מַמָּשׁ" וְהַשְּׁלִיחוּת:
— Now to clarify the dispatching of "actual angels":
אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁם בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה עה, יא):
— Later in Bereishit Rabbah (75:11) it is taught:
"דָּבָר אַחֵר: 'וַיִּשְׁלַח וְגוֹמֵר' – לָמָּה שָׁלַח וְכוּלֵי? אָמַר: אֶשְׁלַח שְׁלוּחִים אִם יַחֲזוֹר בִּתְשׁוּבָה", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— "Another explanation: 'And Jacob sent messengers'—why did he send them? Jacob thought: I will send messengers to see if he will repent, see there;
מַשְׁמָע שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ הָיָה לְהַחֲזִירוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
— indicating that Jacob's intent was to bring Esau to repentance.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם לִפְנֵי זֶה עַל פָּסוּק "אֶל עֵשָׂו אָחִיו" – "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עֵשָׂו, הוּא אָחִיו",
— And this explains the Midrash's comment on "unto Esau his brother"—"even though he is the wicked Esau, he is his brother",
רָצָה לוֹמַר דְּאַף שֶׁהוּא רָשָׁע גָּמוּר בַּפּוֹעַל, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא אָחִיו חָשַׁב: אֶפְשָׁר דְּגַם בּוֹ יֵשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב;
— meaning that even though Esau was thoroughly wicked in deed, since he was his brother Jacob thought: perhaps in the depths of his heart holiness still abides;
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א): "שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת וְכוּלֵי וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי";
— in the manner of: "it is our true will to do Your will, but what prevents us? The leaven in the dough";
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ (בְּעֵירוּבִין כא עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "הַדּוּדָאִים נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ" – דְּגַם רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִים עֲתִידִים לִיתֵּן רֵיחַ טוֹב;
— and as they expounded on "The mandrakes give a fragrance": that even the wicked of Israel will ultimately yield a sweet scent;
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו" – "רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו".
— and in Bereishit Rabbah (65:22): "He smelled the fragrance of his garments (begadav)—the fragrance of his betrayers (bogedav)."
וְזֶהוּ בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְלֹא יִדַּח נִדָּח, דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא".
— Now this principle belongs definitively to the seed of Jacob whose bed is whole, where none is cast away and a sinner remains Israel.
וְעֵשָׂו נִקְרָא (בְּקִדּוּשִׁין יח עַמּוּד א): "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר",
— And Esau is halakhically designated in Kiddushin (18a) as an "apostate Israelite" (Yisrael mumar),
כִּי נוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מִיִּצְחָק וְרִבְקָה כְּיַעֲקֹב;
— for he was conceived in sanctity from Isaac and Rebecca just like Jacob;
אֶלָּא שֶׁאָז הָיָה עֲדַיִן בְּיָדוֹ לָצֵאת מִשֵּׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— except that in that era it was still possible for him to sever himself completely from the lineage of Israel;
וְרַק מִיַּעֲקֹב הִתְחִיל זֶה דַּאֲפִילּוּ מוּמָר נִקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל דָּבָר.
— this permanence starting only with Jacob, from whom onward even an apostate remains an Israelite in all regards.
וְחָשַׁב הוּא דְּגַם יִצְחָק מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְשֶׁגַּם בְּעֵשָׂו כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא אָחִיו פְּנִימִיּוּתוֹ טוֹב.
— And Jacob initially thought that Isaac's bed was likewise whole, and that Esau's inner core was fundamentally good.

p: וּבִפְרָט שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁיִּצְחָק אֲהֵבוֹ;
— Especially so since Jacob saw that Isaac loved him;
וְאִיתָא בְּתַנְחוּמָא (תּוֹלְדוֹת סִימָן ח) שֶׁצָּדוֹ בְּפִיו,
— and it is taught in Tanchuma (Toldot 8) that Esau trapped him with his mouth,
שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁבָּא מִבֵּית הַתַּלְמוּד – "לֹא כָּךְ הֲלָכָה מִן כָּךְ וְכָךְ? לֹא כָּךְ אִיסּוּרוֹ? לֹא כָּךְ הֶתֵּירוֹ?",
— saying: I have returned from the academy—is this not the halakhah regarding such-and-such, its prohibition, and its permission?
דְּמִזֶּה נִרְאֶה שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ חָכְמָה יְתֵירָה:
— showing that Esau possessed extraordinary intellectual brilliance;
דְּהַגַּם שֶׁהָיָה כָּל הַיּוֹם בַּשָּׂדֶה וְשָׁקוּעַ בְּתַאֲווֹתָיו וְלֹא עָסַק כְּלָל בַּתּוֹרָה,
— for even though he spent his days hunting in the field immersed in lust, never studying Torah,
יָדַע לְכַוֵּון הַהֲלָכָה בִּטְעָמֶיהָ וּבִפְרָטֶיהָ כְּאִילּוּ עָסַק בָּהּ כָּל הַיּוֹם!
— he could deduce the halakhah with its precise rationales as though he had toiled in it all day!
דְּיִצְחָק זָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה הָיָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּיוֹמָא כח עַמּוּד ב), וְיָדַע כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ מֵאָבִיו;
— For Isaac was a venerable sage presiding in his academy (Yoma 28b), possessing the entire Torah from Abraham;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּגַם הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר הַהֲלָכָה לַאֲמִיתָּהּ מִדַּעַת עַצְמוֹ, הֲגַם שֶׁלֹּא לָמַד כְּלָל;
— so Esau must have derived the halakhah intuitively from his own intellect without study;
וְזֶה חָכְמָה יְתֵירָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ בְּיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁהָיָה "יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים",
— which was an intellectual acumen in Torah that we do not find even in Jacob, who was "dwelling in tents",
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "אָהֳלוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם וְשֶׁל עֵבֶר", שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ לִלְמוֹד וּלְקַבֵּל מֵהֶם, וְלֹא מֵעַצְמוֹ
— expounded as the academy of Shem and Eber, where Jacob had to study and receive from masters, unlike Abraham
כְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁשְּׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו הָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי רֹב חָכְמָתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (שָׁם): "דְּאִיצְטַגְנִינוּת גְּדוֹלָה הָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ".
— whose two kidneys welled forth Torah through his great wisdom, as stated in the cited passage: “great astrological knowledge was in his heart” (Yoma 28b).

Whenever Esau entered the house, he would ask his father: ‘My father, is one obliged to tithe for salt?’ Isaac would exclaim in amazement: ‘Observe, how scrupulous this son of mine is concerning the commandments!’ And when his father would ask him: ‘Where were you today, my son?’ ‘At the house of study,’ the youth would reply and he would add: ‘Is this not the law under certain circumstances; are not these things prohibited and these permitted?’ By such remarks, he entraped his father with his mouth. That is why he loved him. …”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 28b: “When they were in Egypt there was a yeshiva with them, as it is stated: ‘Go and gather the Elders of Israel’ (Exodus 3:16), indicating that there were Sages among them who studied Torah. And similarly, when they were in the desert, there was a yeshiva with them, as it is stated: ‘Gather for me seventy men from the Elders of Israel’ (Numbers 11:16). Abraham our Patriarch was himself an Elder and would sit in yeshiva, as it is stated: ‘And Abraham was old, advanced in years’ (Genesis 24:1). From the apparent redundancy of the terms old and advanced in years, it is derived that old means that he was a wise Elder and prominent in Torah, and advanced in years means that he was elderly. Similarly, Isaac our Patriarch was an Elder and sat in yeshiva, as it is stated: ‘And it came to pass when Isaac was old and his eyes were dim’ (Genesis 27:1). Similarly, Jacob our Patriarch was an Elder and sat in yeshiva, as it is stated: ‘And Israel’s eyes were heavy with age’ (Genesis 48:10).”

p: וּכְבָר אָמַרְתִּי עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "זָרַח מִשֵּׂעִיר לָמוֹ, הוֹפִיעַ מֵהַר פָּארָן" (דְּבָרִים לג, ב),
— And I have already explained the verse: "He shined forth from Seir unto them; He beamed from Mount Paran",
שֶׁאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בָּלָק קצב עַמּוּד ב) דְּשָׂרִים שֶׁלָּהֶם נָתְנוּ עוֹד נִבְזְבְּזָא דִּילְהוּ (מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם) לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
— where the Zohar states that the guardian angels of Esau and Ishmael gave gifts (nivzeveza) to Israel,
וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ מַהוּ הַזְּרִיחָה וְהַהוֹפָעָה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵהֶם.
— though it was not explained what that shining and beaming consisted of.
אֲבָל כְּלַל הַדָּבָר: מָצִינוּ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם חָכְמָה,
— However, the general principle is: we find that wisdom exists among the nations,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בִּבְרָכוֹת נח עַמּוּד א) שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עַל חַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם: "שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לְבָשָׂר וָדָם",
— as taught in Berakhot (58a) that over gentile sages we recite: "Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood",
כְּמוֹ עַל חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק דִּבְחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים "שֶׁחָלַק לִירֵאָיו",
— just as over Jewish sages, except that for Jewish scholars we say: "Who has imparted of His wisdom to those who fear Him";
לְפִי שֶׁהֵם יְרֵאָיו, וְיִרְאַת ה' הוּא אוֹצָרוֹ שֶׁל הַחָכְמָה,
— because they fear Him, and fear of God is the treasury of wisdom (Isaiah 33:6),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת לא עַמּוּד א): "דְּאִי לָאו – לָאו, וּמוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ",
— for if one has wisdom without awe, it were better he had not acquired it,
כִּי בְּלֹא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁהַחָכְמָה תַּתְעֵהוּ עוֹד עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ סַם הַמָּוֶת,
— since without fear of Heaven wisdom misleads him until it becomes a potion of death,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם פח עַמּוּד ב) לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ, וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים אֵינוֹ לוֹ סַם חַיִּים.
— serving as a deadly drug to those who turn left, and certainly not a potion of life.
כִּי בְּחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא תּוֹרָה – דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא מוֹרֶה לוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ יֵלֵךְ,
— For among Jewish sages wisdom is Torah—meaning it instructs (moreh) the path one must walk,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נֵר לְרַגְלִי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קה), וְהוּא חַיֵּינוּ;
— as it is written: "Your word is a lamp unto my feet" (Psalms 119:105), and it is our very life;
וְאָז נִקְרָא חֵלֶק מֵחָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמִסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּתַנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא לד);
— and then it is termed an imparted portion of His divine wisdom, His living words and inner mysteries;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמַת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אֵינוֹ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹרֶה לְלִבּוֹ כְּלוּם,
— whereas the intellect of the nations is not Torah, for it does not morally guide the heart,
וּכְחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם, שֶׁהִכִּיר מַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָדַע הָאֱמֶת, וְעִם כָּל זֶה יָעַץ עֵצוֹת לְהַכְשִׁילָם וְנֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— like the wisdom of Balaam, who knew the truth of Israel yet advised how to ensnare them.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי ב, יג):
— And therefore our Sages taught (Eichah Rabbah 2:13):
"אִם יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ: יֵשׁ חָכְמָה בֶּאֱדוֹם – תַּאֲמֵן, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: 'וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם' (עֹבַדְיָה א, ח);
— “If they tell you: There is wisdom in Edom—believe it, as it is written: ‘Shall I not destroy the wise men out of Edom?’;
יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בֶּאֱדוֹם – אַל תַּאֲמֵן, דִּכְתִיב: 'בַּגּוֹיִם אֵין תּוֹרָה' (אֵיכָה ב, ט)".
— if they tell you: There is Torah in Edom—do not believe it, for ‘among the nations there is no Torah’”.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר "אֱדוֹם", מַשְׁמָע דְּבוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחָכְמָה דְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, וְכָל חַכְמֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִל"ה (מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים וְחָמֵשׁ) אוּמּוֹת שֶׁיּוֹנְקִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
— And specifying Edom demonstrates that in Edom resides the primary root of gentile intellect, nourishing all thirty-five nations on the left.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (בִּמְגִילָּה טז עַמּוּד א): "הָאוֹמֵר דְּבַר חָכְמָה מֵאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי – מֵחֲכָמָיו דְּהָמָן",
— And so they said in Megillah (16a): “Whoever says a word of wisdom even among the nations is called a sage—derived from the wise men of Haman”,
וְהֵם זֶרַע עֵשָׂו, דְּמִסְּתָמָא חֲכָמָיו הֵם מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ;
— who were of the seed of Esau, his sages being from his kinsmen;
וְהַחָכְמָה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הָאֱמֶת, דְּ"אִם מִזֶּרַע הַיְּהוּדִים מָרְדֳּכַי וְגוֹמֵר" (אֶסְתֵּר ו, יג),
— and their wisdom lay in perceiving the truth: “If Mordechai be of the seed of the Jews, you shall surely fall before him”,
וְאַף שֶׁהִשִּׂיגוּ זֶה, לֹא הִכְנִיעוּ עַצְמָם לְמָרְדֳּכַי, כִּי מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְשְׁכוּ אַחַר רְצוֹן לִבָּם נֶגֶד הַחָכְמָה, דְּאֵינוֹ תּוֹרָה לְהוֹרוֹת לַלֵּב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— yet despite perceiving this they did not humble themselves before Mordechai, continuing to follow their heart’s malice contrary to their intellect, because it was not Torah that guides the heart.

p: וְגַם מָצִינוּ: "חֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת" (מִשְׁלֵי יד, לד), שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם מִדַּת חֶסֶד,
— And we also find that the nations possess the trait of lovingkindness,
וְהוּא מִיִּשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁהוּא פְּסֹלֶת הַחֶסֶד דְּאַבְרָהָם,
— which flows from Ishmael, the dross of Abraham’s Chesed,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ לְכָל אוּמּוֹת הַיּוֹנְקִים מִמֶּנּוּ,
— permeating all thirty-five nations on the right;
וְאֶצְלָם הוּא "חַטָּאת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא (דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא י עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁכָּל כַּוָּנָתָם לְהִתְיַהֵר וּלְקַנְטֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּשְׁאָר כַּוָּנוֹת רָעוֹת;
— being termed "chattat" (sin), because their charity is performed for arrogance and to taunt Israel;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ: "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה" (יְשַׁעְיָה כז, יא) שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם שָׂכָר.
— yet the Sages noted that they receive temporal reward in this world.

p: וְחָכְמָה דְּעֵשָׂו הוּא מִפְּסֹלֶת הַגְּבוּרָה דְּיִצְחָק,
— And the wisdom of Esau derives from the dross of Isaac’s Gevurah,
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה קָא אָתְיָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פ עַמּוּד ב);
— for the Torah emerges from the side of Gevurah (Zohar III 80b);
וְהַתּוֹרָה נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יז, ה),
— and the Torah is an unripe drop of Supernal Wisdom (Bereishit Rabbah 17:5),
וְזֶהוּ הַנִּבְזְבְּזָא דִּיְהָבוּ חֶלְקָם.
— and this was the gift (nivzeveza) that Esau and Ishmael yielded to Israel.
וּמִשֵּׂעִיר הָיָה זְרִיחָה גְּמוּרָה,
— And from Seir (Esau) came a radiant shining,
דִּכְשֶׁבָּא הַחָכְמָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל נַעֲשָׂה תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹר;
— for when that raw intellectual capacity was incorporated into Israel, it was transformed into Torah which is pure light;
וְעַל כֵּן רַבִּי מֵאִיר יָצָא מִנֵּירוֹן קֵיסָר שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵשָׂו (גִּיטִּין נו עַמּוּד א),
— and therefore Rabbi Meir was descended from Nero Caesar who was of Esau (Gittin 56a),
וְאִיתָא (בְּעֵירוּבִין יג עַמּוּד ב) דְּנִקְרָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁמֵּאִיר פָּנִים בַּהֲלָכָה, וְלֹא הָיָה בְּדוֹרוֹ כְּמוֹתוֹ;
— and it is taught (Eruvin 13b) that he was called Rabbi Meir because he illuminated the eyes of the Sages in halakhah, having no equal in his generation;
וְהוּא יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דִּסְתָם מִשְׁנָה – רַבִּי מֵאִיר (סַנְהֶדְרִין פו עַמּוּד א),
— and he is the foundational pillar of the Oral Torah, an unattributed Mishnah reflecting Rabbi Meir,
וּמִשְׁנָיוֹת הוּא כּוֹלֵל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְהוּא חָכְמַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי אֶצְלוֹ נַעֲשָׂה הַחָכְמָה תּוֹרָה.
— and the Mishnah encompasses the Oral Torah, for within him intellect was consecrated into holy Torah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Kedoshim 1:6-3:13: “As R. Jose was once on the road he met R. Hiya and said to him: ‘In reference to the verse, ‘Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for evert’ (I Sam. 3, 4), the Companions, you know, have stated that it will not be purged with sacrifices nor offering, but it can be purged with words of Torah. Why is this? Because the words of the Torah rise above all offerings.’ He replied: ‘This is truly so, and if a man studies the Torah it benefits him more than all sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and even though punishment has been decreed against him from above it is annulled. Therefore it is that words of the Torah are not susceptible to uncleanness, because it can itself purify those who are unclean. We know this from the verse: ‘The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever’ (Ps. 19, 9).’ Said R. Jose: ‘But it says here ‘the fear of the Lord’, and not ‘the Torah’?’ He replied: ‘It means the same thing, because the Torah comes from the side of Geburah (Might).’ Said R. Jose: ‘Rather derive it from here: ‘The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom’ (Ibid. 111, 10). It is written: ‘The fear of the Lord is pure’,’ and the Torah is called ‘holiness’, as it is written, ‘I the Lord am holy’, and the Torah is the supernal holy Name. Therefore he who studies it is first purified and then sanctified. We have learnt that the holiness of the Torah surpasses all other sanctifications, and the holiness of the superior recondite wisdom is highest of all.’”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 17:5: “‘The Lord God cast a deep slumber upon the man, and he slept. He took one of his sides, and He closed it with flesh in its place (taḥtena)’ (Genesis 2:21). ‘The Lord God cast (hipil) a deep slumber’ – Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi: The beginning of downfall (mapala) is sleep. When a person sleeps, he does not toil in Torah and does not do any work. Rav said: There are three slumbers: the slumber of sleep, the slumber of prophecy, and the slumber of a trance. The slumber of sleep – ‘the Lord God cast a deep slumber upon the man, and he slept.’ The slumber of prophecy – ‘it was when the sun was setting, and a deep slumber fell upon Abram’ (Genesis 15:12). The slumber of a trance – ‘No one saw, and no one knew, and no one awoke, as they were all asleep, because a deep slumber from the Lord had fallen upon them’ (I Samuel 26:12). The Rabbis said: There is also the slumber of foolishness, as it is written: ‘For the Lord poured upon you a spirit of deep slumber’ (Isaiah 29:10). Rabbi Ḥanina bar Yitzḥak said: There are three microcosms; sleep is a microcosm of death; a dream is a microcosm of prophecy; Shabbat is a microcosm of the World to Come. Rabbi Avin adds another two: The orb of the sun is a microcosm of the supernal light; Torah is a microcosm of the supernal wisdom.”

The Rabbis said: There is also the slumber of foolishness, as it is written: ‘For the Lord poured upon you a spirit of deep slumber’ (Isaiah 29:10). Rabbi Ḥanina bar Yitzḥak said: There are three microcosms; sleep is a microcosm of death; a dream is a microcosm of prophecy; Shabbat is a microcosm of the World to Come. Rabbi Avin adds another two: The orb of the sun is a microcosm of the supernal light; Torah is a microcosm of the supernal wisdom.”

h: The Power of Torah to Reveal Merit

p: וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה עה, יג) אָמַר:
— And in Bereishit Rabbah there (end of §75):
דְּדוֹרוֹן שֶׁשָּׁלַח (יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו) לְסַמּוֹת עֵינָיו,
— the lavish gift that Jacob sent to Esau was to blind his eyes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים" (דְּבָרִים טז, יט) –
— as it is written: "For a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise" (Deuteronomy 16:19)—
וְאֵין חֲכָמִים אֶלָּא אֲדוֹמִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהַאֲבַדְתִּי חֲכָמִים מֵאֱדוֹם וְגוֹמֵר".
— and "wise" refers specifically to Edomites, as it is said: "Shall I not destroy the wise men out of Edom?"
וְאֵין רָצָה לוֹמַר דַּאֲחֵרִים לֹא נִקְרְאוּ חֲכָמִים;
— Now the Midrash does not mean that others cannot be termed wise;
רַק רָצָה לוֹמַר: חֲכָמִים כָּאֵלּוּ שֶׁהַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּור עֵינֵיהֶם – זֶהוּ רַק אֲדוֹמִים,
— rather it means: sages whose intellect is entirely swayed by bribery—that is uniquely the Edomites,
שֶׁחָכְמָתָם נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר הַנְּגִיעָה שֶׁבְּלִבָּם, וִיכוֹלִים לְהַטּוֹת חָכְמָתָם כִּרְצוֹנָם וּלְטַהֵר הַטָּמֵא.
— for their wisdom is held hostage to personal bias, enabling them to twist their intellect to declare the impure pure.
וְזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן חָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּעֵירוּבִין שָׁם יג עַמּוּד ב);
— This was also Rabbi Meir’s wisdom, as stated in Eruvin 13b;
וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה צֹרֶךְ וְתוֹעֶלֶת לְמִי שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַר;
— and there is a profound necessity for this dialectic power to defend one who has already sinned;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: "אִלּוּ הָיִינוּ בַּסַּנְהֶדְרִין לֹא נֶהֱרַג אָדָם מֵעוֹלָם", כִּדִתְנַן בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּמַכּוֹת (ז עַמּוּד א),
— in the manner of Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva who declared: "Had we been in the Sanhedrin, no man would ever have been executed" (Makkot 7a),
כִּי הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לִמְצוֹא זְכוּת גַּם עַל עֲבֵירָה גְּמוּרָה,
— because they could uncover an angle of merit even for an actual transgression,
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם, וְשָׁם (יא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "הָיָה לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים שֶׁיִּגָּמֵר דִּינוֹ לִזְכוּת";
— and as stated in Makkot (11b): the High Priest should have prayed that their judgment be sealed for innocence;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה חַיָּיב גָּלוּת בֶּאֱמֶת עַל פִּי דִּין,
— and even though according to strict letter of the law he deserved exile,
אֲבָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵין לָהֶם סוֹף, וַחֲכָמִים גְּדוֹלִים יוּכְלוּ לִמְצוֹא זְכוּת גַּם לִמְחוּיָּב גָּמוּר.
— words of Torah are boundless, and great masters can reveal merit even for someone truly liable.
וְכֵן בִּתְפִלָּה הָיָה פּוֹעֵל שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם, וְזֶהוּ "לַמַּיְמִינִים בָּהּ" (שַׁבָּת פח עַמּוּד ב).
— And likewise through prayer he moved Hashem to illuminate their eyes, which is the path of those who turn to the right.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "פִּיהָ פָּתְחָה בְחָכְמָה וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ" (מִשְׁלֵי לא, כו).
— And concerning this it is stated: "She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the Torah of lovingkindness is upon her tongue" (Proverbs 31:26).

paragraphs.text: Makkot 7a: “The mishna continues: The mitzva to establish a Sanhedrin with the authority to administer capital punishments is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael. A Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seven years is characterized as a destructive tribunal. Since the Sanhedrin would subject the testimony to exacting scrutiny, it was extremely rare for a defendant to be executed. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: This categorization applies to a Sanhedrin that executes a transgressor once in seventy years. Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva say: If we had been members of the Sanhedrin, we would have conducted trials in a manner whereby no person would have ever been executed. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In adopting that approach, they too would increase the number of murderers among the Jewish people. The death penalty would lose its deterrent value, as all potential murderers would know that no one is ever executed.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88b: “And that is what Rava said: To those who are right-handed in their approach to Torah, and engage in its study with strength, good will, and sanctity, Torah is a drug of life, and to those who are left-handed in their approach to Torah, it is a drug of death. Alternatively, why are matters of Torah referred to as royal? Because to each and every utterance that emerged from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, two crowns are tied. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘My beloved is to me like a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts’ (Song of Songs 1:13)? The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, even though my beloved, God, causes me suffering and bitterness, He still lies between my breasts. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interpreted the verse: ‘My beloved is to me like a cluster (eshkol) of henna (hakofer) in the vineyards of (karmei) Ein Gedi’ (Song of Songs 1:14). He, Whom everything (shehakol) is His, forgives (mekhapper) me for the sin of the kid (gedi), i.e., the calf, that I collected (shekaramti) for myself. The Gemara explains: From where is it inferred that the word in this verse, karmei, is a term of gathering? Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said that it is as we learned in a mishna: A launderer’s chair upon which one gathers (koremim) the garments.”

— Yet Esau used his intellect destructively to descend to the grave,
וְכָפַר בָּעִיקָּר וּבִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, וּמָכַר הַבְּכוֹרָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז עַמּוּד ב);
— denying the Creator and the resurrection of the dead, and selling the birthright;
שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סג, יד) שֶׁהִכְנִיס כַּת פָּרִיצִים וְאָמַר לָהֶם וְכוּלֵי וְנִיחֲכוּ עָלָיו,
— for in Bereishit Rabbah (63:14) it is taught that Esau brought in a gang of scoffing scoundrels who laughed at Jacob,
כִּי הֶחֱזִיק אֶת יַעֲקֹב לְתָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ חָכָם בָּזֶה שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִקְנוֹת הַבְּכוֹרָה לְעִנְיַן שֶׁיַּקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹת,
— mocking Jacob as a simpleton for seeking to purchase the sacrificial privileges of the birthright,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם דְּעַל כֵּן קְנָאָהּ יַעֲקֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— as the Midrash explains that Jacob bought it specifically to offer sacrifices;
וְעֵשָׂו בְּחָכְמָתוֹ הָיָה זֶה לִשְׂחוֹק וּלְלֵיצָנוּת שֶׁיּוּכַל לִקְנוֹת זֶה,
— and Esau viewed the transaction with cynical ridicule, scoffing at how spiritual status could be bought,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֹּאמַר לְכֹהֵן "מְכוֹר כְּהֻנָּתְךָ לִי", כִּי אֵין זֶה דָּבָר הַנִּמְכָּר דְּשַׁיָּיךְ רַק לְזֶרַע אַהֲרֹן;
— just as one cannot tell a Kohen "sell me your priesthood," it being an intrinsic lineage;
וְכֵן בְּכוֹרָה לַעֲבוֹדָה שַׁיָּיךְ רַק לְמִי שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר שֶׁנּוֹלַד רִאשׁוֹן.
— and so sacrificial duty naturally belongs only to the firstborn who emerged from the womb first.
וְסִיְּימוּ שָׁם בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה:
— And the Midrash concludes there:
וּלְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ כִּמְשַׂחֲקִים, הִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְשָׂחַק עִמָּהֶם וְקִיֵּים הַבְּכוֹרָה לְיַעֲקֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— because they treated it as a mockery, the Holy One mocked them in return and ratified the transaction unto Jacob;
כִּי הָאֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב, לִהְיוֹת הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ.
— for absolute Truth aligns with Jacob, establishing the definitive halakhah in his favor.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה לוּרְיָא (מַהַרְשַׁ"ל סִימָן לו)
— And in line with the Responsa of the Maharshal (§36)
לְעִנְיַן אָרֶנְדָּא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּל הָעִנְיָן רַק דִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא, מְהַנֵּי מִדִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא
— regarding business lease-rights (arenda): since the entire matter depends on the law of the kingdom, the transaction takes effect under that law
(וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה בְּהַגָּהַת מָרְדֳּכַי שַׁבָּת, וְתַשְׁבֵּ"ץ קָטָן סִימָן שצח
— and similarly in Hagahot Mordekhai, and Tashbetz Katan §398
לְעִנְיַן כִּבּוּד מוֹהֵל וְסַנְדָּק דִּמְהַנֵּי דְּלֹא יָכוֹל לַחֲזוֹר,
— regarding honoring a mohel or sandak, that one cannot retract
אַף שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר דְּלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ קִנְיָן, מִתּוֹרַת סִיטוּמְתָּא, עַיֵּין שָׁם);
— even though formal property acquisition does not apply, binding under commercial custom (situmta)
; וְאַף קִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כִּשְׂחוֹק, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׂחַק עִמָּהֶם וְהִסְכִּים, הָוֵי קִנְיָן מִדִּינָא דְּמַלְכוּתָא דְּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים.
— so too this sale of the birthright, though mocked as a game, became legally absolute under the supernal royal decree of the King of kings.
וְשָׁם בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה אָמְרוּ: דְּמִיכָאֵל וְגַבְרִיאֵל כָּתְבוּ שֶׁהַבְּכוֹרָה לְיַעֲקֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— And in Bereishit Rabbah they stated that the archangels Michael and Gabriel drafted the deed verifying the birthright to Jacob;
רָצָה לוֹמַר נַמֵּי: שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִמְלַךְ בְּבֵית דִּינוֹ,
— meaning that the Holy One took counsel with His heavenly court,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאַחְאָב: "רָאִיתִי אֶת ה' וְגוֹמֵר וְכָל צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם עֹמְדִים עָלָיו מִימִינוֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ" (מְלָכִים א כב, יט),
— as written regarding Ahab: "I saw Hashem sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right hand and on His left",
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּנְחוּמָא שְׁמוֹת יח): "מַיְמִינִים (לִזְכוּת) וּמַשְׂמְאִילִים (לְחוֹבָה)";
— which our Sages expounded: "those on the right arguing for merit, and those on the left arguing for guilt";
וְהֵם שְׁנֵי מַלְאָכִים אֵלּוּ: זֶה מִיָּמִין – רֹאשׁ כִּתּוֹת הַמַּיְמִינִים (מִיכָאֵל), וְזֶה מִשְּׂמֹאל (גַּבְרִיאֵל).
— these being the two archangels: Michael on the right leading the advocates of merit, and Gabriel on the left.

paragraphs.text: Teshuvot Maharshal 36: “It is known throughout the kingdom that customs rights and similar privileges, distilled spirits, and other governmental franchises in a city are acquired through a written arenda lease, and on this basis they adjudicate… The sages also treated something that is not an ordinary sale as a complete acquisition, as in the case of situmta… The principal rule of commercial acquisition follows custom; all the more so the custom and law of the king. Therefore, in my opinion, one who purchases customs rights or the like from the king, even before the term begins, has made a complete acquisition; one who takes it from him commits outright robbery, recoverable in court.” The responsum concerns the legal effectiveness of customary government leases. Rav Tzadok invokes its principle of acquisition by accepted law and custom.

paragraphs.text: Tashbetz Katan 398: “Maharam said: One who promises his fellow that he may circumcise his son or serve as sandak must fulfill his promise. Although a person cannot transfer something not yet in existence, here it is customary for people to promise their sons to one another for circumcision or sandak and to fulfill it. Since situmta acquires by custom, here too the custom must be fulfilled… Rabbi Yechiel of Paris, however, said that a promise made while the woman is pregnant has no effect, for the child is not yet in existence. Custom applies where a formal acquisition could take effect; we have not found that custom effects an acquisition where a formal acquisition could not.” The passage records both Maharam’s reliance on custom and Rabbi Yechiel’s limitation. Rav Tzadok invokes the former principle.

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְהַטּוֹת לְכָל צַד,
— And this is the dynamic of the Oral Torah, which can be turned in all directions,
וִיכוֹלִים "לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ" – דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר עֲבֵירָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁמְּשָׁלוּהָ לְשֶׁרֶץ,
— being able to "purify the creeping insect"—meaning to uncover hidden merit for an actual transgression,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית טז עַמּוּד א): "טוֹבֵל וְשֶׁרֶץ בְּיָדוֹ";
— as stated: "one who immerses while holding a creeping defilement in his hand";
וּמַה שֶּׁנֶּחְשָׁב כִּשְׂחוֹק, יְכוֹלִים לִמְצוֹא טְעָמִים לְזַכּוֹת וּלְקַיֵּים.
— and that which was deemed a joke can be shown to possess profound legal validity.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 16a: “§ Similarly, Rav Adda bar Ahava said: A person who has a transgression in his hand, and he confesses but does not repent for his sin, to what is he comparable? To a person who holds in his hand a dead creeping animal, which renders one ritually impure by contact. As in this situation, even if he immerses in all the waters of the world, his immersion is ineffective for him, as long as the source of ritual impurity remains in his hand. However, if he has thrown the animal from his hand, once he has immersed in a ritual bath of forty se’a, the immersion is immediately effective for him.”

p: וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא כְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב –
— Now our father Jacob, peace be upon him, embodies the totality of the Written Torah—
כִּי מֹשֶׁה מִלְּגָאו, יַעֲקֹב מִלְּבַר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן יג) –
— Moses being its inward soul and Jacob its outward manifestation (Tikkunei Zohar 13)—
וְהוּא נִקְרָא "תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת", וְאִיתָא (בִּבְרָכוֹת ה עַמּוּד ב): "אֱמֶת – זוֹ תּוֹרָה",
— and it is titled the "Torah of Truth" (Berakhot 5b),
וְהִיא תּוֹרַת ה' שֶׁאֵין לְהוֹסִיף וְלִגְרוֹעַ בָּהּ אֲפִילּוּ אוֹת אַחַת.
— the Torah of Hashem wherein not a single letter may be added or subtracted.
אֲבָל: "תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ג) – לְהַשִּׂיג הָאֱמֶת מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— However: "The integrity of the upright shall guide them" (Proverbs 11:3)—to extract truth through the Oral Torah,
שֶׁהוּא חָכְמַת חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּקְרֵאת "אֵשֶׁת חַיִל",
— which is the intellect of the Sages of Israel, the Congregation of Israel titled the "Woman of Valor",
מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת – "פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לַהּ".
— the chariot for Malchut: "the mouth, we title it the Oral Torah."
וְעַל יְדֵי הַזְּרִיחָה וְהַהוֹפָעָה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ חָכְמָה וָחֶסֶד מֵעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל –
— And through the shining of wisdom and lovingkindness extracted from Esau and Ishmael as mentioned above—
"פִּיהָ פָּתְחָה בְחָכְמָה", וְאֶצְלָהּ נַעֲשָׂה הַחָכְמָה תּוֹרָה וְנִקְרָא "תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד".
— she opens her mouth with wisdom, and within her that intellect becomes Torah, termed a "Torah of lovingkindness."
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה,
— For the Written Torah emerges from the side of Gevurah,
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִקְרָא תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד;
— whereas the Oral Torah is termed the Torah of lovingkindness;
שֶׁאִיתָא (בְּסֻכָּה מט עַמּוּד ב): "וְכִי יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁל חֶסֶד וְתוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל חֶסֶד? אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה לִשְׁמָהּ – זוֹ הִיא תּוֹרָה שֶׁל חֶסֶד",
— as taught in Sukkah (49b): "Is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah not of kindness? Rather, Torah studied for its own sake is a Torah of kindness",
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רכב עַמּוּד ב): "אֵיזֶהוּ חָסִיד? הַמִּתְחַסֵּד עִם קוֹנוֹ",
— meaning as stated in the Zohar: "Who is pious (chassid)? He who acts with lovingkindness toward his Maker",
וְגַם נֶאֱמַר: "גֹּמֵל נַפְשׁוֹ אִישׁ חָסֶד" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, יז) – שֶׁגּוֹמֵל בָּזֶה חַיִּים לְנַפְשׁוֹ,
— and "The merciful man does good to his own soul" (Proverbs 11:17)—bestowing life unto his soul,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (פח עַמּוּד ב): "לַמַּיְמִינִים בָּהּ – סַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי".
— and as in Shabbat (88b): "to those who turn to its right, it is an elixir of life."

p: וְיָמִין הוּא חֶסֶד;
— And the right is Chesed;
וּמַיְמִין וּמַשְׂמְאִיל שַׁיָּיךְ רַק בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and turning right or left applies strictly to the Oral Torah,
דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּתִיבָא וּמַנְחָא, וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁוִים בָּהּ,
— for the Written Torah is inscribed and immutable, all of Israel sharing it equally,
וְאֵין שָׁם מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן, וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לְקַנְטֵר וְלֹא לְהִתְגָּאוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא כַּוָּנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.
— there being no oral debate, vanity, or taunting applicable to its fixed text.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַסֵּד עִמָּהּ, וְהַחֶסֶד – לִהְיוֹת חָכָם לְהֵיטִיב, וְלֹא לְהָרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
— And one must treat it with piety, using intellect to do good and uncover merit, never to do harm, Heaven forbid.
וּבְחָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מַשִּׂיגִים יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַנְּבִיאִים,
— And through the wisdom of the Oral Torah the Sages perceive deeper mysteries than all the prophets,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא יב עַמּוּד א): "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא", וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַמְבַּ"ן:
— as stated in Bava Batra (12a): "A sage is superior to a prophet," and see there in the commentary of the Ramban.

— Up to here from the author's holy handwriting, the conclusion of the discourse being absent.
וְעִנְיַן "מַלְאָכִים מַמָּשׁ" וְשֶׁ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" נִתְבָּאֵר בַּמַּאֲמָרִים הַבָּאִים בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא:
— And the matter of "actual angels" and that "both these and those are the words of the living God" will be further elucidated in the subsequent discourses with the help of Heaven:
